samples.text:
The charts shows what the students who graduated from two universities, X and Y, were doing six months after they finish their degrees.

In University X, more than half of graduates had a full-time work, it was 58%. Further study was 17% and part-time work was 12%. Only 6% was unemployed and 7% did other things. So most of the graduates from University X were working six months after the graduation.

In University Y, full-time work was also the most common but the percentage was lower, only 41%. Further study was higher than University X with 26%, and part-time work was also higher at 19%. Unemployed was 9%, which is a little more than University X, and other was 5%.

Overall, the graduates from University X was more successful to find full-time jobs. On the other hand, more graduates from University Y decided to continue study or have a part-time job. In both universities the unemployed people was a small group, less than 10%.
samples.why: Clear comparison with accurate figures · overview present but at the end and fairly general · paragraph-by-university organisation is mechanical · adequate vocabulary with some awkward phrasing · several agreement, tense and preposition errors.

samples.text:
The pie charts compare the activities of graduates from two universities, X and Y, six months after they had completed their degrees.

Overall, full-time employment was the most common outcome for graduates from both universities, but it was considerably more prevalent at University X. Graduates of University Y, by contrast, were more likely to be in further study or part-time work.

At University X, well over half of graduates (58%) had found full-time jobs, while 17% had gone on to further study and 12% were working part-time. Only a small minority were unemployed (6%) or doing something else (7%).

At University Y, the proportion in full-time work was much lower, at 41%, which was 17 percentage points below the figure for University X. However, a larger share of Y's graduates were continuing their studies (26%) or had part-time jobs (19%). Unemployment was also slightly higher, at 9%, whereas the percentage in the other category was 5%. In total, 70% of University X graduates were in some form of employment, compared with 60% at University Y.
samples.why: Clear overview of the key differences · main features well supported with accurate figures and valid totals · logical progression · range of cohesive devices · good vocabulary · frequent error-free sentences.

samples.text:
The charts show the destinations of graduates from University X and University Y six months after graduation.

Although full-time employment was the most frequent outcome for both groups, graduates of University X were markedly more likely to have secured a full-time post, whereas those from University Y were more often engaged in further study or part-time work.

Full-time work accounted for 58% of University X graduates but only 41% of their counterparts at University Y, a gap of 17 percentage points. Conversely, further study was considerably more common among University Y graduates (26%, against 17% for University X), and the same was true of part-time employment, at 19% compared with 12%.

The remaining categories were relatively small for both institutions. Unemployment stood at 6% for University X and slightly higher, at 9%, for University Y, while the proportion engaged in other activities was similar, at 7% and 5% respectively. Taking full-time and part-time work together, 70% of University X graduates were employed in some capacity six months after finishing their degrees, compared with three-fifths of those from University Y, indicating a noticeably stronger employment outcome for the former.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected and compared category by category · clear overview · accurate figures with correct derived totals · cohesion managed smoothly · wide, precise vocabulary · varied structures, all error-free.
